reasoning: Set A is the stronger plan for this project. Its RL design is precise and correct: rewards are defined for every world, cut-off is kept apart from terminal so bootstrapping is right for Q-learning, DQN and GAE, and the closed-form golden cases check out (returns 1.75/1.5/1, advantage 1.095, corridor Q 0.729-1.0, table update 0.46). Catch distances are checked against per-step motion so bodies can't pass through each other, and all three stages are laid out as step-by-step ladders (L1-L4, T1-T4 REINFORCE to PPO, P1-P5 with a snapshot pool and cross-play), which fits a learner. Its six milestones depend on each other correctly and M1 is a real vertical slice. A's weaknesses: stale scope text left behind as the plan grew, a few contract/pipeline mismatches (rebuild returns bool, clip_to_wall vs reflect), very bloated packets that paste the whole 75-case tests.md into split tasks, no named signature for the Snake view functions, and a fully serialized wiring chain. Set B reads well and its per-package Phase 0 / spine / system shape is textbook. But it never defines a reward for any world, even though reward shaping is a concept the user named. It adds a reference-library package and per-milestone comparisons nobody asked for, and its brief invents a cloud-GPU budget. M3 depends falsely on M2's Snake comparison. Its lean packets leave out what builders need: the Learner/Transition protocol, the chain2 world definition, a way to build hand-built Snake states, and coordinate conventions. RunWriter has no snapshot method even though run_loop must save snapshots through it, and TC-38's tolerance is statistically flaky.
